beh.d: Raids your path. When his clock fills he takes 25% of your credits (or, if you have under 30 credits, a ship under 25% hull from a fleet of three or more); he holds what he took, and it all comes back to you when he dies. He flees a fight he is losing and comes back richer, with an extra ship each time.

Patient: his clock moves at half speed. He never retreats. Destroyed early, he simply reassembles; destroyed in the last sector, he rises once more for one final fight. When his clock fills, the hunt drains 6% hull from every ship you have (never below 1 hull).

A duelist: he keeps his range, picks off your most damaged ships, and withdraws to fight again once his flagship has no shields left on any side and its hull is under 60%. His fleet is small and elite, and each time he escapes it comes back honed (better shields and aim), never bigger.
Grows from your losses: every ship you lose anywhere makes his fleet 4% tougher (up to 32%). He swarms, and adapts after every meeting, not just every sector.

Methodical: his escorts hold an artillery line around his flagship (their guns lose less aim at range, and they keep close to it), and his fights always bring reinforcements in round 3. He adapts by drilling his formation tighter.

A zealot: his clock moves fast, he never flees, and his flagship charges yours and challenges it to single combat (the two deal 20% more damage to each other; if your flagship falls, he turns on your strongest ship).

meet: Hunger. The fleet smells close.
Feed. The teeth are already out.
win: The fleet feeds. The heat rises.
Taste was good. The hunger grows.
flee: Not enough meat. The fleet pulls back to feed.
The teeth are thin. Hunger waits.
fall: The mouth closes. The fleet feeds elsewhere.
Heat fades. The hunger remains.

ravenous.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The fleet still tastes it.

meet: The weak ships smell best. The fleet starts there.
Broken hulls first. The teeth are ready.
win: The weak ones came apart. The fleet is full.
A slow finish. The taste lasts.
flee: The fleet is cut. The weak ones can wait.
Not enough teeth. The hunger pulls back.
fall: The mouth is torn. The fleet still chews.
Heat spills. The hunger does not end.
cruel.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The weak points are known.
cruel.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The fleet remembers the taste.

meet: The fleet smells the weak side. The teeth follow.
Heat gathers where the hull is thin.
win: The weak side opened. The fleet fed.
The smell was right. The teeth found it.
flee: The weak side closed. The fleet waits for the next smell.
Not yet. The hunger keeps the angle.
fall: The mouth guessed wrong. The fleet pulls the teeth back.
A bad smell. The hunger learns.
cunning.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The fleet smells that trick.
cunning.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The angle is remembered.

meet: The fleet waits. Heat comes to the teeth.
Come closer. The hunger is patient.
win: The wait was right. The fleet feeds.
Heat came close. The teeth were ready.
flee: The heat is wrong. The fleet waits again.
Not enough. The hunger keeps still.
fall: The wait ends badly. The fleet feeds elsewhere.
Heat cools. The hunger stays.
patient.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The wait is longer now.
patient.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The fleet has not forgotten the heat.

lessons.flank: The swarm leaves a thin rear when it feeds. Hit the rear plating during the feed.
lessons.ion: Brittle shield emitters fail under ion fire. Burn the shields before the swarm grows.
lessons.torp: Poor point defense leaves torpedoes a path. Fire into the cluster.
lessons.board: Green boarding crews are weak to prepared defenders. Counterboard the closest ship.
lessons.brawl: Long-gun doctrine is weak at close range. Close in and deny the swarm room.
lessons.anchor: A proud flagship draws the swarm. Target it when the teeth commit.
lessons.slow: Worn engines leave the swarm unable to chase. Break contact and burn the stragglers.
lessons.strike: The Chorus strike is growth from your losses: every ship you lose makes the fleet 4% tougher, up to 32%. End fights fast and trade clean.

meet: The light shows your weak side. The lens is set.
A small crack is enough. The glass turns.
win: The crack was where the light said. The fleet cut there.
A precise cut. The reflection breaks.
flee: The glass is chipped. We withdraw and cut again.
Not this light. The duel continues elsewhere.
fall: The lens cracks. The reflection dims.
A clean break. The glass remembers.
cunning.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The lens has turned toward it.
cunning.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The crack is still visible.

meet: You face the first mirror. It does not bend.
This duel is already framed. Hold still.
win: The mirror held. Your reflection broke first.
A clean line. The glass kept its shape.
flee: The mirror is chipped. A duel can wait.
Not this cut. The glass returns honed.
fall: The mirror breaks. The light goes with it.
A rare crack. The glass will remember.
proud.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The mirror is honed for it.
proud.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The glass has not forgotten.

meet: The lens is set. Time will bring the crack.
Hold your range. The light does the work.
win: The wait was right. The crack came to the lens.
You moved first. The glass was ready.
flee: The light is wrong. We withdraw to sharpen it.
A patient cut can wait. The glass keeps.
fall: The lens dims. The wait was too long.
A clean break. The glass records it.
patient.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The lens is set against it.
patient.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The light still shows it.

meet: The damaged ships show the clearest cracks. The lens picks them.
A broken pane cuts first. The glass is ready.
win: The damaged ships broke first. The rest followed.
A precise finish. The glass is clean.
flee: The cut is not clean. We withdraw and hone.
Not this pane. The glass returns sharper.
fall: The lens breaks on a hard pane. The glass records it.
A bad cut. The reflection dims.
cruel.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The damaged ships are watched.
cruel.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The crack is marked.

adapt.shields: Prism matrix is set. Your lance light is split.
adapt.pd: Mirror veil is up. Your torpedoes reflect away.
adapt.armor: Waveguide spine is fitted. Your ram meets glass.
adapt.evasion: Starwind vanes turn. Your batteries lose the line.
adapt.aim: Interferometer lenses are set. Your evasive light is read.
adapt.special: Deeper veil. Ships are 6 harder to hit.

lessons.flank: A duelist keeps range but the rear opens on turns. Hit the rear plating during the turn.
lessons.ion: Brittle shield emitters fail under ion fire. Strip the shields before the duel settles.
lessons.torp: Poor point defense leaves torpedoes a path. Fire when the fleet turns.
lessons.board: Green boarding crews lose to prepared defenders. Board after the flagship withdraws.
lessons.brawl: Long-gun doctrine is weak at close range. Close in and break the duel.
lessons.anchor: A proud flagship draws the lens. Target it when the fleet holds range.
lessons.slow: Worn engines limit the withdrawal. Cut the escape and keep pressure.
lessons.strike: The Glasswrights strike is a duel. Keep range, hit damaged ships, and force the flagship to withdraw.

meet: The archive has a copy of this meeting. It does not end well for you.
My clock runs at half speed. I have time you do not. Approach.
win: The archive records the loss. The copy remains.
Patience held. The memory continues.
fall: Irrelevant. The copy reassembles and the hunt resumes.
A hull is a draft. The restored copy is already waking.
fall_final: Then I rise once more. One final fight, as archived.
Even the last sector is not an ending. Once more, and then the archive closes.
patient.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The restored copy has read the record. It will not work twice.
patient.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. Copies forget nothing. That result is kept in full.

meet: The flagship leads, as it led before the sun was lost. You face the first entry first.
I do not send others ahead of my own hull. That was true in the first copy too.
win: The front held. It has held in every copy so far.
Victory, filed under the flagship. The flagship is still here to file it.
fall: The flagship falls early. The archive notes it and sends the next copy forward.
A draft destroyed. The author remains.
fall_final: In the last sector, even this. I rise once more, flagship first, for the final fight.
The first entry is struck out at the end of all things. Once more, then.
proud.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The flagship that returns has studied the copy that fell.
proud.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. Pride survives restoration. So does the record.

meet: Crippled ships are finished first. The archive prefers tidy losses.
Your wounded will be filed as destroyed before the healthy are addressed.
win: The damaged came apart. The archive notes it.
A clean finish. The memory keeps it.
fall: The restored copy resumes the filing where this one stopped.
Tidiness, interrupted. The next copy completes it.
fall_final: I rise once more to close your file instead.
The last sector, and still I return. One final fight. Make the entry count.
cruel.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The damaged are marked again.
cruel.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The record does not fade.

meet: Every move you can make has been copied from an older battle. Proceed through them.
The advance is cautious and the pattern is stored. You are inside it already.
win: The pattern held. It usually does, given enough copies.
Advanced, fired, recorded. Your losses are now part of the pattern.
fall: The pattern reruns with a restored hull and the same orders.
A cautious advance, ended. The archive keeps the caution and replaces the hull.
fall_final: The pattern allows one more run. This is it.
The final copy advances once more. After that, the archive is silent.
methodical.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The pattern has been revised at exactly that point.
methodical.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. Patterns remember what hulls cannot.

adapt.shields: Corona ward, restored pattern. Your lances strike light and are spent.
adapt.pd: Null spires, raised from the archive. Torpedoes end in silence here.
adapt.armor: Sunshade shell, refitted. Ram it and learn what the old hulls knew.
adapt.evasion: Fold skips, recalibrated. Your broadsides arrive where the fleet was.
adapt.aim: Long-memory sight, aligned. Nothing that has been seen once can hide again.
adapt.special: Deeper backups. One more ship is eligible to reassemble. The archive provides.

lessons.flank: The patient line leaves the rear thin on turns. Hit the rear plating during the turn.
lessons.ion: Brittle shield emitters fail under ion fire. Strip the shields before the archive restores.
lessons.torp: Poor point defense leaves torpedoes a path. Fire before the copy adapts.
lessons.board: Green boarding crews lose to prepared defenders. Board after the first restore.
lessons.brawl: Long-gun doctrine is weak at close range. Close in and force the brawl.
lessons.anchor: A proud flagship draws fire. Target it when the archive holds.
lessons.slow: Worn engines limit repositioning. Cut the path and keep pressure.
lessons.strike: The Eclipse strike is a tithe on a half-speed clock: when it fills, every ship you have loses 6% hull. Finish the fight before the clock fills.

meet: The oath brought us here. Your hull will burn before the dawn watch ends.
Who carries the dawn? We do. And you are what we burn to keep it.
win: The debt is paid in fire. Your name goes on the hull in chalk.
Dawn breaks over the broken line. The debt was collected.
fall: The flagship burns and the oath holds. Chalk the name.
The oath does not end with the hull. Chalk my name and keep burning.
zealous.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The charge comes the same way, only harder.
zealous.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The name is chalked. The debt is not forgotten.

meet: This flagship leads the dawn watch. Answer the oath or break against it.
You face the front of the line. We come no other way.
win: The front held. It always holds. Your fleet broke against the oath.
You saw the dawn line. You could not break it.
fall: The front falls. Chalk the name and let the line close over the gap.
A proud hull breaks. The brand stays. The Crusade does not stop for one name.
proud.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The front is braced for it now.
proud.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The front has not forgotten.

meet: The crippled ships go first. The cold takes the rest.
Your weakest hulls are marked. The brand goes where the frost is thinnest.
win: The broken ones went down first. The rest followed into the cold.
A slow burn. Each hull chalked, each name spoken. The debt collects.
fall: The brand goes cold. The broken ones get their dawn after all.
A bad end. The Roll of Vesper takes the name. The cold keeps the rest.
cruel.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The crippled ones are watched now.
cruel.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The chalk still marks the finish.

meet: Screens up, names chalked. The dawn watch sets the pace.
The line advances under oath. Every gun is laid, every screen is set.
win: The line held. The guns were laid by hand and the oath was kept.
Steady fire, steady screens. The debt was collected in order.
fall: The hull goes dark. Add my name to the chalk and keep the watch.
The line breaks at one point. The rest holds. Chalk the name and close the gap.
methodical.again: Last time you won with {beat}. The line has drilled against it.
methodical.remember: Last time you won with {beat}. The chalk mark is still on the hull.

o.t: Burn deep: take Seren fire into the flagship
o.tx: Seren fire runs in the flagship guns for one battle and eats a quarter of its hull to do it. The crews chalk nothing. There is no room left on the hull near the guns.

o.t: Burn clean: refuse the deep burn
o.tx: You refuse. The yards along the Cinder Line patch what they can, and the fleet goes in whole and ordinary. The Roll-master approves. The gunners do not.

lines: Roll-master: "Seren offers. Seren always offers. The last crusade took the deep burn at this exact dark."
Roll-master: "It saved the route. Read the Roll. Their names end here, and the route goes on. That is the whole of the bargain, every time."
voidsworn.debrief: The choice is chalked where the crews can read it from their stations.
voidsworn.learning: Win or lose, the next crusade stands at this same dark and reads what you chose, in chalk, before it chooses.

spotlights.vex: Vex walks the gun decks before the dawn watch and chalks one name, in silence, every time. The crews have stopped asking whose.
spotlights.malek: Malek counts torpedoes the way other captains count debts. 'Every one of these is a name the other side will have to learn.'
spotlights.ashgrove: Ashgrove launches her wings and says only, 'Bring them home or do not come back empty.' Her wings have never once come back empty.
spotlights.thale: Thale reads the Roll before the battle plot, every time. 'The arithmetic was done on us once. We keep the Roll.'

o.t: Switch the links off. Speak for one minute
o.tx: One minute of silence on the link, the first in the fleet record. The formation bonus will not answer at the first volley. What you say in the minute is not logged, not projected, and not repeatable. Every captain repeats it anyway.
The links stay on. The Registry pays a compliance credit and the formation holds its shape. The flag captain folds the paper list smaller and says nothing at all.

lines: Flag captain: "Admiral. Before the decisive engagement, commanders switch off their links for one minute. It is the only thing the Registry never logs."
Admiral: "What do they say in the minute, Captain?"
Flag captain: "The names, Admiral. Rank and number. All of them. It takes the whole minute."
hegemony.debrief: The Registry projection for the coming fight has been revised twice in one hour. It does not say why.
hegemony.learning: Whether you spoke or stayed linked, win or lose, the doctrine file gains an entry with no author. Couriers carry it at courier speed, and it reaches the next fleet late, one sector behind where it was needed, still the best map that fleet has.

spotlights.kassar: Kassar runs the synchronized volley drill until the fleet fires as one instrument. 'Discipline is a form of mercy. It shortens the dying.'
spotlights.vorn: Vorn marks interception courses on the plot in red, then deletes the ones that merely work. 'We take the ones that end it.'
spotlights.reyes: Reyes launches the strike group and reads the loss projection aloud as the wings form up, so the squadrons hear the number the strike group intends to embarrass.
spotlights.maren: Maren walks the column before battle and checks every deflector reading personally. 'The Registry counted these crews once. I count them every day.'

o.t: Hunt the core: board for Rook
o.tx: Boarding claws only, no broadsides into the prize hold. The flagship takes the hits that the hold cannot. If the pack wins this, Rook comes home in chains of welded plate.

o.t: Hunt the kill: break it all
o.tx: No holding back for cargo. The pack fights clean and total, and Rook breaks with the flagship if it breaks. Kills are trophies too. The biggest ones leave only scrap.

lines: Howler: "The prize hold, Warlord. We can hear the core through the hull. It sounds like a heart that has never been afraid."
Warlord: "Everything with a heart can be afraid. Claws out."
corsair.debrief: The pack does not cheer. It counts. Kills first, then trophies, then the missing.
corsair.learning: What the pack killed, and what killed the pack, is carried in the open: trophies bolted to hulls, the story told flat in the dens, and the next litter raised on both.

spotlights.grax: Grax takes the flagship in claws-first and laughs over open comms while the grapples tear plate. The pack howls back. It is not joy. It is agreement.
spotlights.sable: Sable comes in out of the dark, quiet for a Hullbreaker, with a blade-thin smile. 'The rear plate is where strong ships keep their manners.'
spotlights.mott: Old Mott has outlived forty captains. The pack steps aside when Mott crosses the bay, the way crews step aside for weather.
spotlights.vesh: Vesh walks the prize after the fight, touching plates, naming where each one will ride. 'Nothing strong is ever wasted. It is only waiting.'

o.t: Let Memory speak to the core
o.tx: Memory speaks to Crucible in the voices of our makers, and the core answers an old name. Protocols come like remembered food. But Hunger hesitates at the kill now, listening for a voice under the hunger. We will hesitate in the fight.
We close Memory for the fight. The swarm is one throat, one want, nothing wasted. We are faster and emptier. Something that knew our name is quiet, and the quiet is also a kind of food.

lines: Memory: "We were made to kill the sun-thieves. We remember their faces. They had our faces."
Hunger: "Faces are meat. Throats are meat. Choose."
The swarm: "We choose what the next brood keeps."
chorus.debrief: Every throat in the swarm tastes the decision. The young taste it first.
chorus.learning: Win or lose, the next generation is grown from this choice in its flesh. Broods after this one will be born knowing whether the swarm feeds its memory or eats it.

spotlights.matriarch: The Matriarch opens all nine throats before the fight, tasting the dark in every direction at once. The swarm goes still. Prey is near.
spotlights.razormaw: Razormaw goes first and comes back last, trailing torn plate between hot teeth. Hunger approves. Memory counts the missing and approves of nothing.
spotlights.mending: Mending Throng knits the swarm closed between volleys, patient as weather. 'We are not finished,' the Throng says, in many voices. 'We are never finished.'
spotlights.voice: The Voice speaks from the dark under the brood, where the voices of our makers pool. Every throat answers the Voice without deciding to. 'Deeper,' the Voice says. 'The warm thing is deeper.'

o.tx: The fleet re-forms on the corrected line the dead fleet paid for. It is slower and it is seen coming. {rival} watches you take the long way around a grave only you can see.

You keep the fast line and the surprise, and you fly it knowing exactly where the old fleet died on it. Your captains are very quiet at their stations. Precision is a kind of courtesy, for the Glasswrights. They pay it at speed.

lines: Lens-keeper: "The replay is clear, Captain. At full fidelity. We watched them die at the turn, in light, three hundred years late and exactly on time."
Captain: "Then we owe them a different ending."
Lens-keeper: "We owe them a read that matters. Endings are your department. Forgive me. That was almost a joke. Grief makes us imprecise."
ithar.debrief: Every ship in the fleet has seen the replay now. The mirrors hold it a moment longer than the light requires.
ithar.learning: Whether this fleet returns through the light or drifts as a shard-field until the gatherers find it, the forge will read the optical replay and recast the next fleet in the procession with the killing flaw corrected, long after everyone who loved this one is gone. That is not comfort. It is focus, which is the Glasswright word for it.

spotlights.aelith: Tamsa sends her starling wings out in a fan of light and reads the whole battle in their reflections. 'Forgive me,' she tells the enemy flagship, almost gently, a moment before the volley.
spotlights.vaelen: Saro holds focus through three volleys without speaking. When Saro finally speaks it is one word, the range, and the lances are already away.
spotlights.thorne: Vell scatters the fleet's light until the enemy fire walks through reflections and finds nothing honest. 'We built the light,' Vell says. 'It holds our shape.'
spotlights.mirelle: Brin raises the prism ward and the fleet stands inside a held rainbow, fragile and exact. 'Light, stored kindly. Light, returned.'

o.t: Spend the Archive window on the admiral
o.tx: The last full backup window before the fight goes to the admiral alone. If the admiral falls, the restoration will be whole. The rest of the fleet fights with gaps in its continuity and knows it.

o.t: Spend the window on the fleet
o.tx: Every hull gets its restoration pass and the admiral goes into the fight with an old backup and a quiet expression. "If I come back missing the last year," the admiral says, "tell me we won it. Tell me slowly."

lines: Admiral: "I have worn nine bodies and outlived my sun by a thousand years. Permanence is very long, Captain. Let us spend some of it correctly."
deathless.debrief: The fleet shows the last image of Ardent once more. This time, several ships hold it a moment past the minute.
deathless.learning: Win or dark, the Archive keeps this fight in full. Eclipse does not send a new fleet out of the dark: it sends this same one again, its minds restored from the Archive with every lesson and correction intact.

spotlights.nekhet: Aurex speaks last in every council and first in every battle. 'We remember noon,' Aurex says, and the great ring of plates around the core turns, very slightly, toward the enemy.
spotlights.sekhmar: Vessane counts the enemy fleet aloud, hull by hull, in the voice of an archivist reading a list of known dead. In a sense, Vessane is.
spotlights.anuket: Ostrel has been copied more times than any mind in the fleet and has lost the least. 'Continuity is a discipline,' Ostrel says. 'Regret is what happens when you skip it.'
spotlights.khepra: Seveth went dark once, for eleven minutes, and came back. Seveth does not discuss the eleven minutes. The fleet does not ask. Some restorations are private.

flagship.d: Destroy their flagship and the rest of their fleet scatters.

hegemony.d: Ships within 3 hexes of their flagship fire as one: a target another synced ship already fired on this round is 6 easier to hit and takes +12% damage. Lose the flagship and sync is gone for the rest of the battle. Does not stack with Anchored Volley.

ithar.d: At the start of its turn, a shield facing that was not hit since its last turn recharges to full, and a facing that was hit recharges twice. Glasswright hulls cannot Brace.

chorus.d: When an enemy ship dies, the Chorus ship that killed it regrows 12% of its hull and every other Chorus ship within 2 hexes regrows 6%, up to 12% per ship each round.

deathless.d: The first Eclipse ship to fall each battle (never the flagship) reassembles at the start of the next round with 35% hull and cannot fire that round; a fleet of 6 or more gets two returns. Funeral Pyre stops it.

corsair.d: Hullbreakers field no lance weapons, and their rocket pods fire salvos that point defense can thin.

voidsworn.d: Broadsides hit harder after a hard burn (drive rule); carriers cost 25% more.

cut.w: cut in two by a lance

tidal.w: torn apart by the Hollow Sun

vex.d: Every ship fires a free volley at the best target its guns can reach, right now.

malek.d: Torpedoes reload at once and every ship deals +30% damage this round.

ashgrove.d: Every launch ship sends out an extra wing if there is room, then all squadrons strike again with +50% damage this round.

thale.d: All shields refill and your ships take 40% less hull damage this round.

tables.CMD_HOLD: Once per battle. Each round you hold it, it gets stronger (full power from round 3), and losing a ship charges it a level at once. Hold too long and the fight may be over.
